questionLatex: Pulleys A, B, C and D are linked together using a belt, while pulleys C and D are linked using a crossed belt. Pulleys A and E are of the same size, while pulleys B, C and D are of the same size and half of the bigger pulleys. What will be the rotation and speed of the pulley at E relative to the pulley at A if the pulley at A is rotating counter clockwise?
explanationLatex: Pulleys A and B rotate in the same direction, and since B is half the size of A, B spins twice as fast. Pulleys B and C are the same size, so C spins at the same speed and direction as B. The crossed belt between C and D reverses the direction of D relative to C, but since D is the same size as C, their speeds are equal. Finally, pulleys D and E rotate in the same direction, and since E is the same size as A (and thus twice the size of D), E spins at half the speed of D. Combining these, E spins at the same speed as A and in the same direction.
